name: rebuild-4k-hdr
description: A 4K file whose real detail is only 1080p (a 2x up-scaling container): drop to the native grid, rebuild 2x with Real-CUGAN, then semantic HDR -> scRGB -> JPEG XR. Measured on the source this pipeline was written for: 3840x2160 anime still, LANCZOS 1/2 round-trip PSNR 52.9 dB (i.e. the 4K pixels carry 1080p of information), median high-pass noise sigma 1.4/255, no 8/16-pixel blockiness.

stages.note: path comes from `imgen run -i FILE` unless params.path is set
exact 2x area average: undoes the container's own interpolation so the SR model sees native pixels instead of a resampled blur
cheap here (1080p) and before the SR pass, so the model cannot amplify contour steps; measured: smooth-area mean|dx| 0.445 -> 0.375 with lap_abs 4.24 -> 4.21 (no detail loss)

stages.label: rebuild-2x
stages.note: models-pro/up2x-no-denoise: source measured clean, so denoise would only soften; model resolution-denoise happens inside the network
OFF by default: Real-CUGAN already restores line energy (lap_std 15.3 vs 2.6 for the soft 4K input), and unsharp pushes it to 19.0 with visible overshoot — enable only for a deliberately crisp look
the SDR deliverable: the rebuilt 4K image with no HDR grade applied
LumiPic (FLUX.2-klein-base-4B + LoRA). Model/LoRA/interpreter are auto-discovered under tools/LumiPic and .venv; the result is cached as .npy so hdr.map can be re-tuned for free

knee/rolloff are measured, not default: LumiPic's scene-linear field for this dark frame is p50 0.08 / p99.7 0.67 / p99.99 50, so the 2.6 knee the bright-wallpaper pipelines use would leave 0.0008% of pixels lit. At 0.5/1.5 the specular sparkles and the light shafts reach 190-290 nit with an 871 nit peak, 3.2% of pixels affected. Re-tuning needs no GPU (semantic cache)
